To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the variability in the sea surface CO 2 fugacity ( f CO 2 ) is mainly determined by sea surface temperature during the cooling and warming seasons and by the upwelling index during upwelling episodes, while the uptake of carbon by phytoplankton masks the increase in the concentration of inorganic carbon.
the sea surface CO 2 fugacity over the continental shelf of Galicia was mainly controlled by sea surface salinity and sea surface temperature during spring and autumn.

sea-air CO2 exchange in the Galician shelf is controlled by a complex interplay of different factors (upwelling intensity, temperature and salinity) which are influenced by the local meteorological conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the short-term (seasonal) variability of the sea-air CO  exchange of CO2 in the Galician coastal waters.
the study of the variability of the fCO2 and the CO2 fluxes in a coastal upwelling region.

the variability of surface CO2 concentrations and sea-air CO2 exchanges in the shelf waters off the Galicia region, a coastal area characterized by a strong upwelling system and a complex topographic configuration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the continental shelf off the Galician coasts is a net sink of atmospheric CO2, with an average annual uptake of ~0.2 mol C m−2 yr−1.
the Galicia coastal upwelling is a CO2 sink, but the magnitude of the uptake is variable depending on the meteorological and oceanographic conditions.

, in general, the Galician shelf is a net sink for atmospheric carbon dioxide, although the intensity and duration of this sink is influenced by the intensity and duration and the number of upwelling and downwelling periods, the meteorological conditions during the winter and the fresh water inputs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sea-air CO  2 fluxes are controlled by the balance between biological and physical processes.
the sea-air CO  fluxes are mainly controlled by the seasonal cycle of the surface temperature and salinity.

the variability in the surface CO2 fluxes over the shelf waters off the Galicia is mainly driven by the seasonal changes in the SSS, SST and photosynthetic activity of phytoplankton, which mask the effect of the upwelling events on the surface fCO2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Galician shelf acts as a sink of atmospheric CO2, and this sink is more intense during the upwelling period.
the seasonal cycle of fCO2 and sea-air CO2 exchange is mainly controlled by the interaction between upwelling events and the seasonal cycle of SST and SSS.
the Galician coastal ecosystem acts as a sink for atmospheric CO2.
